questions.q: I am a non-executive director of a company. A complaint under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act has been filed against the company and me. The complaint only says that I was 'in charge of and responsible for the conduct of the business of the company'. Can the complaint against me be quashed?

Section 141 NI Act: is a bare averment that a director was in charge of the company enough to proceed against a non-executive director for a dishonoured cheque, or must the complaint say what his role was?
My company's cheque bounced. I am a director but I do not look after the daily running of the company, and I have got a court notice in the cheque bounce case. Can I be made to face the case?
A cheque was given as security for a loan and it bounced when the lender presented it. Can the lender file a case under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act?
Does a security cheque attract section 138 of the NI Act if the debt was not yet due when the cheque was presented?
I gave a blank cheque to someone as security for a loan. They presented it and it bounced and now they have sent me a legal notice. Is a cheque bounce case valid against me?
